tier_reason: First-party Baidu benchmark (docs/cn/benchmark.md, charts dated 2016-01-22/24) comparing brpc against gRPC release-0_11 and Apache Thrift 0.9.1 with CPU models and test parameters stated, but no compiler/flags and no public harness for the gRPC/Thrift servers, so it stays C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Page text: pooled brpc (baidu-rpc_mc) reached the highest throughput in the test, 2.3GB/s; gRPC 'was at the bottom in almost every test it took part in' and its cross-machine multi-client latency CDF 'is completely out of control' (the same-machine CDF test is where some gRPC requests timed out). Read off the charts (derived from page data): same-machine 16B requests, brpc single-connection ~216k QPS vs gRPC ~33k (~6.5x) and thrift_mc ~71k (~3x); 1KB requests at 256 client threads, brpc ~291k vs gRPC ~32k (~9x) and thrift_mc ~70k (~4x); cross-machine 32 clients, brpc ~950k vs gRPC ~39k (~24x) and thrift_mc ~93k (~10x). Versus Thrift the win is not uniform: thrift_mc and UB beat brpc at 1-8 client threads, and single-connection brpc falls below thrift_mc at 16KB+ requests (pooled brpc stays above). The page says Thrift's cross-machine average latency is clearly higher than brpc's.
corrections.hardware: Single machine: E5-2620 @ 2.00GHz, 24 cores with hyper-threading, 64GB RAM, Linux 2.6.32. Cluster 1: 15x E5-2420 @ 1.90GHz + 8x E5-2620 2.0GHz, 12 cores no HT, 1GbE. Cluster 2: 30x E5-2620 v3 @ 2.40GHz, 12 cores no HT, 96GB RAM, 10GbE.
corrections.caveats: Tests were run in 2015/early 2016 (charts timestamped 2016-01-22..24) and the page itself says they may not reflect the latest status. gRPC tested was release-0_11 (pre-1.0) and Thrift was an internal build of 0.9.1, so neither represents modern versions. gRPC was left out of the two multi-server latency tests. Compiler and build flags are not stated and the gRPC/Thrift server code used is not published. Thrift beats brpc at low client-thread counts (1-8) and against single-connection brpc at 16KB+ requests.

notes: Metadata verified via gh: Apache-2.0, not archived, not a fork, 17,620 stars, last commit 2026-09-26 (active). The record's Thrift sentence was inverted: brpc is ~3x Thrift at small requests and single-connection brpc falls behind Thrift at large ones; the 'timeouts' belong to the same-machine CDF, not the cross-machine one. The English docs/en/benchmark.md is an untranslated stub pointing to the Chinese page.

tier_reason: Author's own h2load runs of examples/helloworld, with full logs in issues/PRs and the Apple M1 Max CPU stated, but no compiler or build flags for grpcxx or gRPC C++. The gRPC v1.48.4 row comes from a 2023-10-29 run on a different machine and macOS than the grpcxx v0.2.0 run. That makes it first-party with partial methodology, so tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README benchmark table (req/s, h2load unary hello world): scenario 3b (100 clients x 10 streams), grpcxx v0.2.0 libuv single-threaded 452k vs gRPC C++ v1.48.4 callback 142k (~3.2x, derived from page data). gRPC's best cell is 152k in 2b, where grpcxx does 449k (~3.0x, derived from page data). README says '3x faster compared to the official implementation(s)'. In the same table grpc-go v1.56.2 peaks at 308k and tonic v0.10.2 at 212k (both 3b). In the only same-machine comparison (PR #2), grpcxx multi-threaded commit 4b13fce reached 346k (2b) and 355k (3b) vs gRPC 152k and 142k (~2.3-2.5x, derived from page data). The asio backend is slower: 114k-290k in 3b.
corrections.hardware: MacBook Pro 2021, Apple M1 Max, 32GB RAM. grpcxx v0.2.0 ran on macOS 14.2.1 (23C71) (issue #25). The gRPC v1.48.4 and grpc-go rows come from PR #2 (2023-10-29), and issue #20 says that device and macOS differ from the later runs.
corrections.caveats: Author's own benchmark. The README table mixes runs: the gRPC C++ and grpc-go rows come from PR #2 on a different M1 Max device and macOS than the grpcxx v0.2.0 rows (issue #20 warns of this). h2load settings also differ (gRPC: --requests=100000; grpcxx v0.2.0: --duration=3). PR #2 warns that single-threaded h2load may cap near ~300k req/s. Compiler and build flags for the C++ builds (grpcxx and gRPC) are not stated. gRPC v1.48.4 is an older release; the benchmark is a trivial hello-world unary call.

notes: Issue #25 (the original benchmark_url) shows only grpcxx v0.2.0 numbers (452k etc.), not gRPC; the README Benchmarks table is the page that puts gRPC and grpcxx side by side, so benchmark_url was changed to it. The record's pairing of 452k (3b) with 152k (gRPC's 2b cell) was relabeled; ~3x still holds. Metadata verified: MIT, not a fork, not archived, 115 stars, last commit 2026-05-19 (active).

tier_reason: First-party README charts (docs/images/benchmark1-6.png) state the CPU (Xeon E5-2630 v3), RAM, NIC and test parameters. The harness is public in benchmark/ (server.cc, client.cc, thrift_server.cc on Apache Thrift TNonblockingServer). No compiler or version is stated and flags appear only in build files, so it is not A. It is first-party, so not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Read off README charts (derived from page data). Same machine, 1024B requests (benchmark3): SOGOU srpc-std ~310k QPS vs 'FACEBOOK thrift-binary' (Apache Thrift TNonblockingServer per benchmark/thrift_server.cc) ~145k at 32 client threads (~2.1x) and ~309k vs ~191k at 256 threads (~1.6x). Same machine, 100 threads, by request size (benchmark1): ~319k vs ~185k at 16B (~1.7x) to ~254k vs ~158k at 16KB (~1.6x) and ~205k vs ~133k at 32KB. Cross-machine: srpc ~470-520k vs ~167-220k at 64-1024 threads (benchmark2, ~2.3-2.8x); ~310k-670k vs ~145k-222k at 1-16 client processes (benchmark4, ~2.1-3.0x). Latency CDFs at fixed QPS (benchmark5/6): srpc stays under ~170us to the 99.9th percentile same-machine while Apache Thrift sits at ~235-480us; cross-machine Thrift is ~3.8ms+ at p80. SRPC's own thrift-binary server beats Apache Thrift by a little more (~331k vs ~145k at 32 threads). Versus Baidu brpc, srpc-std is slightly slower same-machine (~310k vs ~346k at 32 threads) but faster cross-machine (~520k vs ~405k; ~670k vs ~407k).
corrections.workload: Echo RPC with empty responses, driven by SRPC's own async client (benchmark/client.cc) against each server: same-machine QPS vs client threads (1-256, 1024B) and vs request size (16B-32KB, 100 threads); cross-machine QPS vs client threads (64-1024, 32B) and vs client processes (1-16 x 32 threads, 32B); latency CDFs at fixed QPS with 1% slow outliers (same-machine 10k QPS 1024B; cross-machine 32 clients x 2500 QPS 512B). Compared: SOGOU srpc-std, SOGOU brpc-std, SOGOU thrift-binary, BAIDU brpc-std and 'FACEBOOK thrift-binary' (Apache Thrift TNonblockingServer, TBinaryProtocol, 16 IO + 16 worker threads).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated in the README. benchmark/CMakeLists.txt (2020 initial commit) builds SRPC's benchmark as CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE RelWithDebInfo with -Wall -fPIC -pipe -std=c++11 -fno-exceptions (now -std=c++17). A comment in benchmark/GNUmakefile builds the Thrift server with 'g++ ... -O2 -g -std=c++11'. No compiler version is given.
corrections.caveats: Project's own benchmark. Values are read visually off PNG charts, not a numeric table. The chart label 'FACEBOOK thrift-binary' is the Apache Thrift C++ TNonblockingServer (benchmark/thrift_server.cc uses apache::thrift, TBinaryProtocol, 16 IO + 16 worker threads), not fbthrift. The Thrift version is not stated; the server code uses boost::shared_ptr and PosixThreadFactory, which point to an older Apache Thrift. All servers are driven by SRPC's client, so only server-side speed is compared. Responses are empty. Compiler is not stated. The charts date from the 2020 open-source release. srpc-std is slightly slower than Baidu brpc on the same-machine tests.

notes: The record's numbers match the charts. I fixed the caveat that guessed the baseline was Facebook's own Thrift: the harness shows it is Apache Thrift's TNonblockingServer, which matches the record's baseline field. I also widened the workload to all six charts and added the build flags from benchmark/. Metadata verified: Apache-2.0, not a fork, not archived, 2,143 stars, last commit 2026-09-15 (active).
